title: The unresolved-worker-count refusal names the escape that works
action: The concurrent-worker git guard denies through two arms (checks.rs:653-681). The `count > 1` arm hands back CONCURRENT_TREE_TEMP_INDEX_REMEDY (paths.rs:365-372), which ends with the sentence that actually unblocks a caller: "A genuinely path-scoped `git commit -- <your paths>` is allowed too." The Unresolved arm (checks.rs:655-669) substitutes a one-line remedy naming only `.bee/reservations.json`, so a session that hits it is told to repair a file and never told it can simply land its work path-scoped — even though paths.rs:317-326 already exempts that form in BOTH arms. Keep the unresolved arm's own remedy: naming the corrupt store is the right first move for a solo session, and the comment at checks.rs:663-667 explains why it was deliberately made different. Append the path-scoped-commit escape to it rather than replacing it with the temp-index recipe. Do not touch the `count > 1` arm, do not touch classify_concurrent_tree_verb, and do not add any new exemption — this cell changes refusal text only, no control flow. Extend `concurrent_tree_guard_unresolved_arm_names_the_reservation_store` (tests.rs:701) so it keeps its existing two asserts and gains one proving the escape sentence is present.

truths: The unresolved arm's refusal still names .bee/reservations.json and the inspect/restore remedy
The unresolved arm's refusal also names the allowed path-scoped `git commit -- <paths>` escape
The count > 1 arm's refusal text is byte-identical to before
No control flow changes: the same invocations deny and allow as before
